lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn presents the core grammar rule in a clear, visual format. It explicitly contrasts the use of 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negative sentences.
Look for students focusing on the table and their ability to answer simple check questions (e.g. ‘Which word is for positive sentences?’).
“Today, I need some word magicians! We're going to learn a very important grammar rule about two small but tricky words: 'some' and 'any'. Let's look at the table to learn the secret.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - B. Circle and number

details: Circle and number provides the first controlled practice of the grammar rule. Students choose the correct quantifier ('some' or 'any') and match the sentence to the corresponding picture.
Look for correct circling of 'some' or 'any' based on the sentence type, and accurate numbering of the pictures.
“Great, you know the rule! Now I need your help to check these sentences. Can you circle the correct word and then match the sentence to the right person?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - C Make the sentences negative

details: Make the sentences negative gives students practice in grammatical transformation, rewriting positive sentences as negatives.
Look for accurately rewritten sentences, with correct negative verb forms and the correct use of 'any'.
“Now for a challenge! All of these sentences are positive. I want you to be word magicians and change them into negative sentences for me.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - D Make the sentences positive

details: Make the sentences positive provides further practice in grammatical transformation. Students rewrite negative sentences as positives, changing the verb form and correctly using 'some'.
Look for correctly formed positive sentences, with the correct verb forms and the appropriate use of 'some'.
“You did a great job with the negative sentences. Now let's do the opposite! Can you use your magic to change these negative sentences back into positive ones?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.120-122 - A Find ay and oy words

details: Find... strengthens recognition of the target phonics words. Students scan the word search to locate the words quickly and accurately, reinforcing their visual memory of the spellings.
Look for correct identification and circling of all the target words within the word search grid.
“For this challenge, the 'ay' and 'oy' words are hiding in a puzzle! I need my best word magicians to help me find them all.”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.120-122 - B Write the words

details: Write the words gives students controlled practice spelling the phonics words they located. It reinforces the word-picture connection and neat handwriting.
Look for correct spelling of each word, accurate matching to the pictures, and neat letter formation.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.120-122 - B Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops reading fluency and comprehension. Students follow along with the audio, connecting the written words to the story's events and the spoken narration.
Look for students following the text with their finger, paying attention to the story and showing understanding of the main events.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.120-122 - D Say the story with your friends

details: Say the story with your friends provides fluency practice through retelling. Students work in groups to narrate the story in their own words or act out the dialogue, building speaking confidence.
Look for confident retelling of the main story points, active participation within the group and clear pronunciation.
